questions.text: In the network 200.10.11.144/27, the fourth octet (in decimal) of the last IP address of the network which can be assigned to a host is ____________.
questions.solution:
/27 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] blocks of 32 addresses. 144 lies in the block 128 to 159.

159 is the broadcast address, so the last usable host is 158.

Answer: 158

questions.text: Consider a network connecting two systems located 8000 kilometers apart. The bandwidth of the network is 500x[latex]10^{6}[/latex] bits per second. The propagation speed of the media is 4x[latex]10^{6}[/latex] meters per second. It is needed to design a Go-Back-N sliding window protocol for this network. The average packet size is [latex]10^{7}[/latex] bits. The network is to be used to its full capacity. Assume that processing delays at nodes are negligible. Then, the minimum size in bits of the sequence number field has to be ___________.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]T_p=\frac{8\times10^6}{4\times10^6}=2[/latex] s
- [latex]T_t=\frac{10^7}{5\times10^8}=0.02[/latex] s

Window for full use = [latex]1+\frac{2T_p}{T_t}=1+200=201[/latex]. Go-Back-N needs at least W + 1 = 202 sequence numbers.

[latex]2^8=256\ge202[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 bits

Answer: 8

questions.text:
Consider the following reservation table for a pipeline having three stages S1,S2 and S3.

The minimum average latency (MAL) is ________.
questions.solution:
Forbidden latencies: S1 is used at 1 and 5 (gap 4); S2 at 2 and 4 (gap 2). Forbidden = {2, 4}, collision vector = 1010.

- Latency 3 again and again: CV stays 1011 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] cycle (3), average 3
- Cycle (1, 5): average 3

MAL = 3

Answer: 3

questions.text:
Consider the following code sequence having five instructions I1 to I5. Each of these instructions has the following format.

OP Ri, Rj, Rk

where operation OP is performed on contents of registers Rj and Rk and the result is stored in register Ri.

I1: ADD R1, R2, R3
I2: MUL R7, R1, R3
I3: SUB R4, R1, R5
I4: ADD R3, R2, R4
I5: MUL R7, R8, R9

Consider the following three statements.
S1: There is an anti-dependence between instructions l2 and l5
S2: There is an anti-dependence between instructions l2 and l4
S3: Within an instruction pipeline an anti-dependence always creates one or more stalls

Which one of above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Anti-dependence (WAR): a later instruction writes a register an earlier one reads.

- S1: I2 and I5 both write R7, which is output dependence, not anti [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False
- S2: I2 reads R3 and I4 writes R3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] anti-dependence [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- S3: in an in-order pipeline WAR causes no stall [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: Only S2 is true

Only S2 and S3 are true

questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: segment 1 adds X[0][i] = i, and segment 2 adds X[i][0] = i. Same Y [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- S2: X[0][0], X[0][1], ... are one row, contiguous in row-major order [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- S3: X[0][0], X[1][0], ... are n elements apart [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: Only S1 and S2 are correct
